findings.title: Upsampled count drops null weights and truncates
findings.body: upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) and is substituted for count() on allowlisted error queries. There is no ifNull or if(sample_weight > 0, sample_weight, 1) fallback; the comment says null checks were removed on purpose. In ClickHouse, sum skips nulls and returns 0 when every value is null, and toInt64 truncates toward zero, so a fractional weight such as 1/0.3 becomes 3. Allowlisting a project does not backfill existing rows, and events that were not client-sampled commonly have a null or 0 sample_weight. Those events disappear from the total, so turning the feature on can collapse an error chart from the real count to 0 or a large undercount. default_result_type is also "number" rather than "integer", so the count series meta type changes for clients that requested count(). Nothing in this PR computes an upsampled weight of 1/sample_rate either, so the new stats test's expectation of 10 for a 0.1 client rate is not what this aggregate implements.

findings.title: Test helper writes sample_rate, not sample_weight
findings.body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling copies contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate into normalized_data["sample_rate"] (0.1 in the new stats test). The aggregate added in this PR sums the sample_weight column, and OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest expects each single event to contribute 10. This helper never sets sample_weight and never stores 1/client_sample_rate. It only runs inside Factories.store_event, after manager.get_data() at line 1049, so it cannot affect a weight already derived during normalize, and it is not on the production ingest path. if client_sample_rate also treats 0 as missing. The event this helper stores does not contain the value upsampled_count reads, so the allowlisted-project test cannot observe a count of 10 unless an unshown insert hook rewrites sample_rate into sample_weight.

findings.title: Error check is a raw substring match
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query lowercases the raw query string and returns true if it contains the substring event.type:error. That is true for queries that are not error-only, including !event.type:error, event.type:error OR event.type:transaction, and a message or tag value that merely contains that text. When it returns true and every project is allowlisted, count() is rewritten to sum(sample_weight). The helper itself says sample_weight does not exist for transactions. Those queries then either fail in ClickHouse with a missing column or count non-error events as 0 because null weights are skipped by sum. A user asking for non-error totals can get a 500 or a silently zeroed chart. The unit test only covers the exact strings event.type:error and event.type:transaction, not negation or mixed filters. Parse the search syntax and apply the rewrite only when the query is exclusively error events.

findings.title: Eligibility cache key uses process-randomized hash()
findings.body: The allowlist cache key is built with Python's built-in hash() of the project-id tuple. Since Python 3.3 that hash is salted per process via PYTHONHASHSEED, so it is not stable across web workers that share sentry.utils.cache. Each worker reads and writes a different Redis/memcache key for the same organization and projects, so the cache never hits across processes. invalidate_upsampling_cache (line 73) uses the same hash and is never called from allowlist updates, so it cannot invalidate other workers even if it were wired up. hash() can also collide and reuse another project set's boolean. options.get for this allowlist is already an in-process lookup; adding cache.get, and cache.set on every miss, to every organization events-stats request is a remote round trip on a hot path and is slower than the lookup it claims to optimize. Use a stable key (joined sorted ids or a digest) in an in-process cache, or just call options.get.

findings.title: Upsampling check ignores the query actually executed
findings.body: _get_event_stats decides upsampling from the enclosing request dataset and request.GET query, not from scoped_dataset and the query argument it actually runs. get_event_stats_factory calls this helper with scoped_dataset set to discover and with rewritten queries such as (query) AND !event.type:transaction when a metrics-enhanced dashboard widget is split. Those calls still see the outer metrics dataset, and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns false for metrics datasets, so the error probe and the user-visible ERROR_EVENTS result stay on raw count() even when every project is allowlisted. The upsampling decision is therefore not the decision for the dataset and query being executed. Pass scoped_dataset and the query argument into the check.

findings.title: Top-events ranking still uses raw count()
findings.body: When topEvents is set, only timeseries_columns are rewritten to upsampled_count(). selected_columns from get_field_list and orderby from get_orderby are left as count(), and get_equation_list is passed through unchanged on the same call. The top-N query therefore ranks groups by raw event count while the chart plots upsampled weights. Issues or projects with different client sample rates will show the wrong top series, and the plotted values will not match the sort metric. An equation that still contains count() stays on the raw count in the same response as an upsampled count() y-axis. Rewrite orderby, selected aggregates, and equations the same way, or rank with the upsampled aggregate.

findings.title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public function
findings.body: The new upsampled_count SnQLFunction is registered without private=True, unlike the function immediately above it in function_converter. It is therefore a public events-search aggregate: a caller can request yAxis=upsampled_count() or use it in a query without the allowlist or error-dataset checks in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects. That bypasses the gate and runs sum(sample_weight) on projects and datasets the helper explicitly refuses, which either errors or returns undercounts. Mark the function private so only the server-side column rewrite can use it.

findings.title: Transaction upsampling test does not wait for Snuba
findings.body: test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events stores a transaction with store_event and immediately GETs events-stats at this line, without wait_for_event_count. setUp waits for the two error events before querying, which shows ingestion is asynchronous in this Snuba test class. The new transaction may not be visible yet, so the assertion that the first bucket count is 1 fails intermittently. Wait for the transaction to be queryable before asserting.

findings.title: Accidental gitlink added as sentry-repo
findings.body: This change adds a gitlink sentry-repo pinned to a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a, which is the PR base commit, not a dependency of the upsampling feature. Merging a submodule pointer will break clones and CI (missing submodule URL, or a recursive checkout of this same repo) and is unrelated to error upsampling. Remove sentry-repo before merging.
